symptom: Guest tries to vsock-connect to host CID=2 port N but receives VIRTIO_VSOCK_OP_RST. No process is listening on the host UDS at <uds_path>_<N>.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Listener present (LISTEN state on the UDS)

fix_steps.action: Pre-create the host-side AF_UNIX listener BEFORE guest connects
Build a generic per-port spawner on the host (e.g. systemd socket activation on UDS paths)
fix_steps.command: Configure systemd .socket unit for each expected port

symptom: Guest can't reach the internet through the host. Packets from the TAP never make it to the egress interface. Host has IPv4 forwarding disabled.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should be 1; if 0 → root cause

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace whether packets reach the TAP
diagnostic_steps.expected: Outbound packets visible from guest

fix_steps.action: Enable IPv4 forwarding (runtime + persistent)
fix_steps.command: echo 1 | sudo tee /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward; echo 'net.ipv4.ip_forward=1' | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf

symptom: Guest doesn't see /dev/vsock. PUT /vsock attached the device on Firecracker side but guest kernel lacks CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS.

diagnostic_steps.expected: =y or =m
Char device should exist

fix_steps.action: Rebuild guest kernel with CONFIG_VIRTIO_VSOCKETS=y

symptom: After snapshot restore, MMDS GETs return empty/old data. The MMDS data store is intentionally not persisted across snapshots.

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm MMDS configuration survived (only data is dropped)
diagnostic_steps.expected: version, network_interfaces, ipv4_address all preserved; data store empty

fix_steps.action: Orchestrator must reseed MMDS after every restore

symptom: Guest gets connection-refused or no-route when trying to fetch from MMDS at 169.254.169.254 (or configured IP). Guest hasn't added a route for the MMDS IP.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should resolve to a network interface
network_interfaces[] non-empty

fix_steps.action: Add route in guest
Make persistent via init script
fix_steps.command: Add the route command to /etc/network/if-up.d or systemd-networkd config

symptom: Untrusted guest workload (e.g., AI agent fetching arbitrary URLs) reads sensitive metadata from MMDS via SSRF. MMDS V1 has no token requirement.

diagnostic_steps.expected: If 'V1' (or absent → defaults to V1) → vulnerability confirmed

diagnostic_steps.action: Check Firecracker metrics for evidence of token abuse
diagnostic_steps.command: Inspect mmds.rx_no_token + mmds.rx_invalid_token counters in metrics output
diagnostic_steps.expected: Non-zero → workloads accessing without tokens

fix_steps.action: Migrate MMDS to V2 (session-token-required)
fix_steps.validation: MMDS rejects unauthenticated GETs; rx_no_token metric stops growing for new workloads

fix_steps.action: Audit guest workloads to use the V2 PUT-token-then-GET pattern
fix_steps.command: Update guest tooling to issue PUT /latest/api/token first
fix_steps.validation: Guest reads succeed via tokenized path

symptom: Guest packets reach the host's egress interface but have non-routable source IPs. NAT masquerade rule isn't installed.

diagnostic_steps.command: sudo nft list ruleset; OR sudo iptables-nft -t nat -S POSTROUTING
diagnostic_steps.expected: MASQUERADE rule for guest IP/subnet → egress iface
Without MASQUERADE: packets visible with raw guest IP (172.16.x.x — non-routable)

fix_steps.action: Install MASQUERADE rule
fix_steps.command: sudo nft add table firecracker; sudo nft 'add chain firecracker postrouting { type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept; }'; sudo nft add rule firecracker postrouting ip saddr <guest-ip> oifname <egress> counter masquerade; sudo nft add rule firecracker filter iifname <tap> oifname <egress> accept

symptom: Network requests larger than the rate-limiter bucket size are silently never permitted — bucket can't accumulate enough tokens for one request.

diagnostic_steps.expected: size should be ≥ max single request size (typically MTU * burst factor)

fix_steps.action: Increase rate limiter bucket size to exceed any single legitimate request

symptom: VirtIO/net throughput per microVM caps at ~10-15 Gbps despite faster host NIC. TAP backend is single-queue; no IFF_MULTI_QUEUE.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Combined: 1 (single-queue)
Plateau around single-queue limit

fix_steps.action: Scale by adding more microVMs (each with its own TAP)
fix_steps.command: Run N microVMs, distribute load across them

fix_steps.action: Tune host TAP txqueuelen for burst absorption

symptom: Firecracker fails to attach a TAP device with EPERM. Running uid lacks CAP_NET_ADMIN.

diagnostic_steps.expected: CAP_NET_ADMIN should be present (or TAP must be pre-created by privileged user)

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify TAP exists and is accessible
diagnostic_steps.expected: TAP exists; /dev/net/tun rw for uid

fix_steps.action: Pre-create TAP under privileged user; Firecracker only opens, doesn't create
fix_steps.command: sudo ip tuntap add <tap> mode tap user <fc-uid>; sudo ip link set <tap> up

fix_steps.action: Or grant CAP_NET_ADMIN to the binary (less secure)

symptom: Two restored clones of the same snapshot collide on the same vsock UDS path. Second restore fails (or worse: succeeds and steps on the first clone's UDS).

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect both clones' configured UDS paths
diagnostic_steps.expected: Same uds_path → collision

fix_steps.action: Use vsock_override on snapshot/load to give each clone a unique UDS path
fix_steps.validation: Each clone has its own UDS

fix_steps.action: Use jailer per clone — each gets its own chroot, paths are naturally isolated
fix_steps.command: Wrap each FC in jailer with unique --id (which becomes the chroot leaf)

symptom: PUT /vsock fails with ENOENT or ENODEV. Host kernel lacks CONFIG_VHOST_VSOCK module — even though Firecracker bypasses vhost code, the module needs to be loaded.

diagnostic_steps.expected: vhost_vsock available

fix_steps.action: Load the module
fix_steps.command: sudo modprobe vhost_vsock; echo 'vhost_vsock' | sudo tee /etc/modules-load.d/vhost-vsock.conf

symptom: FreeBSD (or other guest) disables Large Receive Offload (LRO), but Firecracker keeps sending 1536+ byte segments anyway. Guest virtio-net device hangs.

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm LRO is being NACKed by the guest driver
diagnostic_steps.expected: off [fixed] when guest doesn't support LRO

diagnostic_steps.action: Capture frame sizes Firecracker is sending
diagnostic_steps.expected: Frames >1500 bytes (LRO-aggregated) when guest expects MTU-sized only

fix_steps.action: Track upstream issue #3905; upgrade to a Firecracker version with the LRO-respect fix
Workaround: switch guest OS to Linux which advertises LRO support
fix_steps.command: Replace FreeBSD guest image with Linux

symptom: Host initiates vsock CONNECT immediately after InstanceStart but Firecracker closes the host-side socket before the guest agent finishes booting and starts listening.

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace timing — when did guest agent listen vs when did host CONNECT
diagnostic_steps.command: Add timestamp logging on both sides; correlate with FC log
diagnostic_steps.expected: Host CONNECT precedes guest listen by N ms

fix_steps.action: Host should wait for a guest-readiness signal before CONNECT
fix_steps.command: Have guest write a sentinel file or send a vsock packet from a known-listening port; host polls before CONNECT

fix_steps.action: Or implement retry-with-backoff on the host CONNECT side
fix_steps.command: Wrap CONNECT in a 100ms-interval retry loop with max 30s timeout

symptom: Active vsock connection terminates mid-flight with a stream read error — Firecracker fails to read from the backing AF_UNIX stream, possibly because the host peer closed it abruptly.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check FC log for backing-stream errors
diagnostic_steps.expected: Error message identifying the failing channel

diagnostic_steps.action: Inspect host peer process state at the time
diagnostic_steps.expected: Peer may have died

fix_steps.action: Make host peers fault-tolerant — close UDS gracefully on shutdown
fix_steps.command: Wrap UDS use in try/finally; explicit close()
fix_steps.validation: Connections close cleanly on peer exit

fix_steps.action: Implement guest-side reconnect logic
fix_steps.command: Guest agent retries vsock connect on EPIPE / ECONNRESET

symptom: PUT /actions {action_type: InstanceStart} returns 400. Required pre-boot resources aren't all configured.

diagnostic_steps.expected: boot-source non-null; machine-config non-null; ≥1 drive

fix_steps.action: Configure each missing resource before InstanceStart
fix_steps.command: PUT /boot-source; PUT /machine-config; PUT /drives/<id> with is_root_device=true; (optional: /network-interfaces, /vsock, etc.); THEN PUT /actions

symptom: Operator attempts to bind the Firecracker API to a TCP port. Firecracker only accepts UDS transport.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Only --api-sock <path> exists; no TCP option

fix_steps.action: Use UDS; bridge to TCP via socat or similar if remote access needed
fix_steps.validation: TCP clients can reach the API; security: protect with firewall + auth proxy

fix_steps.action: For multi-host orchestration, use a per-host control plane that holds UDS local and exposes its own auth'd API
fix_steps.command: Architectural — orchestrator owns the UDS, exposes a tenant-isolated REST/gRPC

symptom: MicroVM with VirtIO balloon overcommitted memory thrashes — guest's effective RAM drops to a tiny fraction (e.g., 8 GiB → 1.4 GiB) causing massive page churn.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check balloon size vs guest available memory
diagnostic_steps.expected: amount_mib should leave guest enough free memory for working set
swap_in / swap_out trending up indicates pressure

fix_steps.action: Deflate the balloon to give the guest memory back
fix_steps.validation: Guest free memory recovers; swap rate drops

fix_steps.action: Set deflate_on_oom=true so balloon auto-deflates under guest OOM pressure
fix_steps.command: PUT /balloon {amount_mib: 0, deflate_on_oom: true, stats_polling_interval_s: 5} (pre-boot only, requires VM restart)

symptom: Production deployment is using a debug-built Firecracker binary. Default seccomp filters are not embedded in debug builds — process runs unsandboxed at the syscall layer.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Release; not debug or experimental-gnu

diagnostic_steps.action: Check Seccomp status as a confirmation
diagnostic_steps.expected: Seccomp: 2; if 0 with no --no-seccomp → likely debug build

fix_steps.action: Replace with release build (musl static)
fix_steps.command: Pull official release tarball or rebuild with --release

symptom: VM with track_dirty_pages=true sees noticeable per-write overhead (small but measurable on write-heavy workloads). KVM page-walk for dirty bits adds cost.

diagnostic_steps.expected: true

diagnostic_steps.action: Benchmark write throughput with and without
diagnostic_steps.command: Run fio random-write workload pre and post
diagnostic_steps.expected: Slight degradation when on

fix_steps.action: If diff snapshots aren't needed, disable track_dirty_pages
fix_steps.command: Pre-boot: PUT /machine-config {..., track_dirty_pages: false}; restart VM

fix_steps.action: If keeping diff snapshots, accept the trade-off — it's by design

symptom: PUT /drives returns 400 with 'Block device backing file does not exist' or InstanceStart fails reading the disk.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check the configured path_on_host (resolved relative to chroot if jailed)
diagnostic_steps.expected: File exists and is readable by the FC uid

fix_steps.action: Copy/bind-mount the backing file into the chroot before PUT /drives
Or pass the file via --bind-mount in your jailer setup script
fix_steps.command: Use a wrapper that mounts the host path into the chroot read-only or read-write
fix_steps.validation: FC sees file at the configured chroot-relative path

symptom: Host crashes; on reboot, guest filesystem is corrupted or 'recently committed' data is missing. Drive was attached with cache_type=Unsafe — guest fsync()s were dropped.

diagnostic_steps.expected: 'Writeback' for any drive holding non-ephemeral data

fix_steps.action: Restart microVM with cache_type=Writeback for persistent drives

symptom: Orchestrator (e2b-style) client process restarts → all live Firecracker sandboxes crash. UFFD handler closure on client exit cascades to FCs that depend on it.

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace the failure chain — which process closure killed which sandboxes
diagnostic_steps.command: Add audit logging on UFFD handler exit → FC death
diagnostic_steps.expected: 1:N relationship visible

fix_steps.action: Decouple UFFD handler lifecycle from client process — run it as a separate long-lived service
fix_steps.command: Architectural: standalone uffd-server process, client only registers FCs with it

fix_steps.action: Or implement UFFD handler reattachment on restart
fix_steps.command: Persist per-FC UFFD state to disk; new handler instance reads on startup
fix_steps.validation: Handler crash + restart leaves FCs running

symptom: Guest clock drifts by ~100-500ms on startup. KVM PTP not configured in guest; guest relies on its initial RTC read which lags.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should exist if CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK_KVM=y

fix_steps.action: Build guest kernel with CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK=y and CONFIG_PTP_1588_CLOCK_KVM=y; configure chrony to use /dev/ptp0
fix_steps.command: Edit kernel config; rebuild; in guest: add 'refclock PHC /dev/ptp0 poll 3 dpoll -2 offset 0' to /etc/chrony/chrony.conf; restart chrony
fix_steps.validation: guest$ chronyc tracking shows /dev/ptp0 source; drift <1ms

symptom: Orchestrator-level health-check failure (Nomad/Consul) triggers a cascade of Firecracker process restarts. The actual fault wasn't with FC.

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify trigger — orchestrator log around the cascade time
diagnostic_steps.expected: Health-check failure entries

diagnostic_steps.action: Differentiate FC fault vs orchestrator fault
diagnostic_steps.command: Per-FC log inspection during the same window
diagnostic_steps.expected: FCs were healthy when orchestrator killed them

fix_steps.action: Tune orchestrator health-check thresholds — allow brief blips
fix_steps.command: Raise Nomad check_restart.limit; widen health-check interval

fix_steps.action: Decouple FC lifecycle from orchestrator restart
fix_steps.command: Use a separate FC supervisor that doesn't restart on orchestrator-level events
fix_steps.validation: Orchestrator can restart independently of FC fleet

symptom: Orchestrator (e2b-style) tries to kill a Firecracker process while UFFD handler is mid-fault-service. Process kill races with handler cleanup → orphaned UFFD state, leaked fds, hung handlers.

diagnostic_steps.command: ps aux | grep uffd-handler; lsof | grep userfaultfd
diagnostic_steps.expected: Zero handlers without a paired Firecracker

fix_steps.action: Sequence kills: SIGTERM Firecracker first, wait for vCPU thread exit, then signal UFFD handler
fix_steps.rollback: Use SIGKILL on both (current racy behavior)

fix_steps.action: Track e2b-dev/infra PR #148 for the canonical lifecycle fix

symptom: Firecracker fails with EMFILE (Too many open files) when starting many devices or under vsock-heavy workload. Each microVM uses 20+ FDs baseline.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Soft limit ≥ 4096 for moderate workloads, much higher for vsock-heavy
≤ soft limit; 20+ baseline

fix_steps.action: Raise via jailer --resource-limit
fix_steps.validation: Limits file shows new limit; Firecracker doesn't hit EMFILE

fix_steps.action: Or systemd unit LimitNOFILE
fix_steps.command: Set [Service] LimitNOFILE=8192 in unit file; systemctl daemon-reload; restart

symptom: Snapshot restore time degrades inexplicably (e.g., 3ms → 8.5ms on aarch64) after host kernel cmdline change. Host kernel logging hot during TAP create — synchronous console writes hold up the FC main thread.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should contain `quiet loglevel=1`; any console=ttyAMA0 / console=ttyS0 is suspect

diagnostic_steps.action: Check dmesg log volume during restore
diagnostic_steps.expected: Few lines if quiet loglevel=1 is set

fix_steps.action: Add quiet loglevel=1 to host kernel cmdline; remove any console= entries

symptom: PUT /machine-config with huge_pages='2M' fails or microVM creates fail under load. Host hasn't reserved enough hugepages.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Reserved >= sum of expected microVM RAM in 2M units

fix_steps.action: Reserve hugepages before starting microVMs
Persist via sysctl

symptom: machine-config.smt is true on a multi-tenant host. Guest sees hyperthreaded siblings via CPUID — speculation side-channel attack surface increases.

diagnostic_steps.expected: false on multi-tenant hosts

fix_steps.action: Set smt=false (pre-boot only, requires VM restart)
fix_steps.validation: guest$ lscpu shows Thread(s) per core: 1

symptom: Jailer fails with 'no internal process constraint' when launched with --cgroup-version=2 + --parent-cgroup pointing at an existing cgroup that has domain controllers in subtree_control.

diagnostic_steps.expected: If non-empty (e.g. 'memory cpu') → root cause

fix_steps.action: Move the jailer to a leaf cgroup (no subtree_control set)
fix_steps.command: Use a different --parent-cgroup that's a leaf, or pass --cgroup args so jailer creates its own subdir

fix_steps.action: Or remove domain controllers from subtree_control
fix_steps.validation: Parent now empty; jailer move succeeds

symptom: Jailer exits with EACCES creating <chroot_base>/<exec>/<id>/root. The chroot base directory or its parents have wrong permissions.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check chroot-base-dir permissions all the way down
diagnostic_steps.expected: Path is writable by the user invoking jailer (typically root)

fix_steps.action: Pre-create with correct perms
fix_steps.validation: Jailer creates the chroot tree successfully

fix_steps.action: Ensure paths aren't writable by unprivileged users (per the prod-host-setup recommendation)

symptom: Multi-tenant host has KSM (Kernel Samepage Merging) enabled. Page-deduplication side channels exploitable — one tenant can detect another's memory contents.

diagnostic_steps.expected: run=0; pages_shared=0

fix_steps.action: Disable KSM and unmerge
Make persistent via systemd unit
fix_steps.command: Add a systemd unit that sets ksm/run=0 at boot; or set kernel.ksm_run=0 sysctl if your distro maps it

symptom: Host CPU usage spikes from kvm-pit kernel threads but the cost isn't accounted to any microVM cgroup. Schedulers undercount per-tenant CPU; noisy-neighbor effects.

diagnostic_steps.expected: kvm-pit/<fc-pid> entries

diagnostic_steps.command: for tid in $(ps -L -o tid= -p <fc-pid>); do cat /proc/$tid/cgroup; done
diagnostic_steps.expected: kvm-pit threads in root cgroup, not microVM cgroup

fix_steps.action: Run an external agent that moves kvm-pit threads into the microVM's cgroup post-start
fix_steps.command: After Firecracker starts, find kvm-pit/<fc-pid> tids and write them to <microvm-cgroup>/cgroup.procs (v2) or tasks (v1)
fix_steps.validation: kvm-pit CPU now accounted to the microVM
fix_steps.rollback: Move them back to root cgroup

fix_steps.action: Or raise the kvm timer-period limit to reduce kvm-pit work
fix_steps.command: sudo modprobe -r kvm_intel kvm; sudo modprobe kvm min_timer_period_us=1000; sudo modprobe kvm_intel; persist via /etc/modprobe.d/kvm.conf
fix_steps.validation: kvm-pit CPU drops; APIC granularity coarsens (workload-test)

symptom: Production Firecracker is started with --no-seccomp (or with a custom filter that whitelists too many syscalls). Defense-in-depth boundary disabled.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should NOT include --no-seccomp; --seccomp-filter only when needed
Seccomp: 2 (filter mode)

fix_steps.action: Remove --no-seccomp from launch script
fix_steps.command: Update orchestrator/systemd unit to drop the flag

fix_steps.action: If a custom filter is needed, audit it; only whitelist what's strictly required
fix_steps.command: Review the JSON; remove unnecessary syscall allowances; recompile via seccompiler-bin

symptom: API call returns 400 with 'cannot be modified after machine startup' or similar. Trying to PUT a pre-boot-only resource (drive, network-interface, vsock, machine-config, boot-source, mmds-config) after InstanceStart.
error_patterns: cannot be modified after machine startup

diagnostic_steps.expected: If 'Running' or 'Paused' → pre-boot resources are immutable

fix_steps.action: Snapshot, destroy, restart fresh microVM with the new pre-boot config
fix_steps.command: PATCH /vm{Paused}; PUT /snapshot/create; SIGKILL; new FC process; load snapshot OR fresh boot with new config
fix_steps.validation: Resource takes effect on the new microVM

fix_steps.action: If only the rate limiter or drive backing file needs changing, use PATCH (those ARE runtime-mutable)

symptom: Multi-tenant Firecracker host has SMT (Hyperthreading) enabled. Speculation-class side channels (Spectre, MDS) become exploitable across tenants.

diagnostic_steps.expected: off; 1

fix_steps.action: Disable SMT at runtime
fix_steps.validation: smt/control shows off; lscpu Thread(s) per core = 1

fix_steps.action: Make persistent: add nosmt to host kernel cmdline

symptom: Host has swap enabled. Under memory pressure, guest memory contents get written to disk → data remanence on disk reuse.

diagnostic_steps.expected: no swap

fix_steps.action: Disable all swap
fix_steps.command: sudo swapoff -a; remove swap entries from /etc/fstab

fix_steps.action: If swap is required, use encrypted swap (LUKS over swap partition)
fix_steps.validation: Swap pages are encrypted at rest

symptom: VirtIO/net TX throughput is lower than expected. Packets get copied twice — descriptor → intermediate buffer → kernel — instead of using scatter-gather.

diagnostic_steps.action: Compare against Firecracker version where scatter-gather was added (PR #2958)
diagnostic_steps.command: firecracker --version; check CHANGELOG for scatter-gather mention
diagnostic_steps.expected: Modern versions include the optimization

fix_steps.action: Upgrade Firecracker to a version >= the PR #2958 release

symptom: Snapshot restore on cgroup-v1 hosts is significantly slower than v2 — restore times of 100ms+ vs 5-15ms on v2.

diagnostic_steps.expected: cgroup2fs (v2) or tmpfs (v1)
>100ms on v1, <20ms on v2 typically

fix_steps.action: Migrate host to cgroup v2 (kernel 5.10+ default on most distros)
fix_steps.command: Add systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1 to host kernel cmdline; reboot

symptom: Snapshot restore fails because CPUID exposed at save time references features unavailable on the restore host (e.g., AVX-512 absent on target).

diagnostic_steps.expected: Save host has features missing on restore host

fix_steps.action: Use a CPU template that targets the LCD across the fleet (e.g., T2 for Intel-broad)
fix_steps.command: PUT /cpu-config with a portable template before save; re-save
fix_steps.rollback: Use no template (lock fleet to identical CPUs)

symptom: PUT /snapshot/load fails with CRC validation error. Snapshot state file is corrupted (interrupted write, disk corruption, transport error).

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify state file size and basic readability
diagnostic_steps.expected: Non-zero size; recognizable header bytes

diagnostic_steps.action: Compute external checksum to compare with the source
diagnostic_steps.expected: Matches the checksum recorded at snapshot-create time (orchestrator's responsibility)

fix_steps.action: Restore from a backup snapshot (orchestrator-managed retention)
fix_steps.command: Pick last-known-good snap.bin + snap.mem from backup

fix_steps.action: Implement mandatory checksum verification in snapshot transport
fix_steps.command: Add SHA256 + signature alongside snap.bin/snap.mem in your storage tier

symptom: PUT /snapshot/create with snapshot_type=Diff returns 400. machine-config.track_dirty_pages was not set to true at boot, so KVM has no dirty bitmap to query.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should be true for diff snapshots; if false → root cause

fix_steps.action: Enable track_dirty_pages BEFORE InstanceStart (it's pre-boot only)
fix_steps.rollback: Drop diff snapshots; use Full only

fix_steps.action: If VM is already running, take a Full snapshot, restore with enable_diff_snapshots=true (re-enables tracking on the restored VM)
fix_steps.validation: Subsequent diff snapshots work on the restored VM

symptom: ARM snapshot restore fails when GIC version differs between save host (e.g., GICv2) and restore host (e.g., GICv3). Device-state mismatch.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check GIC version on both hosts
diagnostic_steps.expected: Should show 'GICv2' or 'GICv3' line — must match

fix_steps.action: Restrict snapshot fleet to a single GIC version
fix_steps.command: Tag/group hosts by GIC version in your scheduler

symptom: Guest crashes mysteriously after restore — page faults can't be served. The MAP_PRIVATE-backed memory file was deleted from the host while the resumed VM was still running.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if mem file still exists
diagnostic_steps.expected: File present and readable
Mapping present and points at a deleted file (shown with '(deleted)')

fix_steps.action: Mark the mem file immutable for VM lifetime in your orchestrator
fix_steps.command: Track per-VM dependency: don't delete mem file until VM process exits
fix_steps.validation: Long-running restored VMs no longer crash on cold pages

fix_steps.action: Use Uffd backend instead — orchestrator-supplied page handler decouples mem file lifetime
fix_steps.validation: Mem file can be retired earlier (or not stored as a file at all)
fix_steps.rollback: Revert to File backend; reinstate file-pinning policy

symptom: After snapshot restore, in-flight TCP connections to the guest break. ARP cache is stale, switches haven't seen the new MAC's frames yet.
error_patterns: no route to host after restore

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm network state is the issue
diagnostic_steps.command: guest$ ip a; ip route; arp -a
diagnostic_steps.expected: Routes present; but external peer ARP cache may be stale

fix_steps.action: Send gratuitous ARPs from the guest immediately on resume
fix_steps.validation: Switch ARP tables refresh; peers can reach guest

fix_steps.action: For multi-clone deployments, give each clone a unique TAP and unique guest IP
fix_steps.command: Per-clone setup: ip netns + ip tuntap add + per-clone NAT rules

fix_steps.action: Design app protocols to be reconnect-tolerant
fix_steps.validation: Resume disruptions are invisible to end users

symptom: Snapshot restore fails (or guest time runs at wrong rate) when source and destination hosts have different TSC frequencies and KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL is unavailable.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Mismatch

diagnostic_steps.command: Check kernel version + try a minimal KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ ioctl
diagnostic_steps.expected: Available on modern kernels

fix_steps.action: Restrict snapshot fleet to homogeneous TSC frequency hosts
fix_steps.command: Tag/group hosts by TSC freq in scheduler

fix_steps.action: Upgrade restore host kernel to one with KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL

symptom: After snapshot restore, MSR_IA32_TSX_CTRL value differs from pre-snapshot. Workload that overwrote this MSR sees the host default after restore. Only happens when no CPU template is in use.

diagnostic_steps.expected: If 'None' (default) → root cause confirmed

diagnostic_steps.action: Check guest MSR pre and post restore
diagnostic_steps.expected: Different values

fix_steps.action: Apply a CPU template that includes MSR_IA32_TSX_CTRL
fix_steps.command: Use static template (T2/T2S) or PUT /cpu-config with custom template containing the MSR

symptom: Restored VM hangs on cold-page access. The userfaultfd handler process crashed or blocked, so page faults from KVM never get serviced.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Process alive; UDS active
vCPU thread blocked in KVM_RUN waiting for page fault completion

fix_steps.action: Restart the UFFD handler with fault-tolerance — it should re-attach to existing FCs via the per-VM UDS
fix_steps.command: Implement: handler process registers with new VMs but also re-binds to existing UDSes on restart
fix_steps.validation: Handler restart doesn't kill running VMs

fix_steps.action: If unrecoverable, kill the FC process and restart from snapshot
fix_steps.command: kill -9 <fc-pid>; orchestrator restarts new FC + new UFFD handler
fix_steps.validation: New VM boots; old session lost

symptom: virtio-block VIRTIO_BLK_T_FLUSH command issued by guest doesn't reach the host kernel block layer. Risk of data loss on host crash even though guest believes data is durable.

diagnostic_steps.expected: cache_type='Unsafe' explicitly drops flushes; 'Writeback' should propagate

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace block layer to confirm FLUSH propagation

symptom: Host dmesg shows 'fc_vmm: page allocation failure: order:6, mode:0x140c0c0' during high-rate microVM creation. KVM cannot allocate large contiguous pages because host memory is fragmented.
